A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Coupled Training study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic experiments and evaluations on Parkinson’s Telemonitoring, Bank Marketing, and PneumoniaMNIST, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The coupled objectives, alternating updates, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The multiplier-scaling correction concerns the derivation. Appendix B.3 clarifies the previously described teacher and post-selection refit without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic linear and logistic scenarios and the same Parkinson’s, Bank Marketing, and PneumoniaMNIST tasks, with unchanged deployment and privileged-feature coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: labeled-only and Two-Stage models, generalized distillation and Vapnik SVM+ for Bank Marketing, and the linear, kernel, and CNN comparisons for PneumoniaMNIST. B.3 clarifies the existing Two-Stage comparison.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, sample sizes, training budgets, tuning grids, and metrics remain unchanged. PneumoniaMNIST’s post-selection ridge refit was already documented in v1; v2 makes the evaluated predictor explicit.

E4.justification: The same privileged-signal, nuisance-dimension, unlabeled-sample-size, and coupling-parameter analyses remain. The Parkinson’s eight-split robustness check and synthetic classification diagnostic are also retained without new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report Bank Marketing averages and 95% confidence intervals across 26 seeds, the same Parkinson’s seed checks, and the five-seed logistic diagnostic. No repeated-run or empirical uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain all scores, confidence intervals, and gains, including coupled Parkinson’s MSE 72.60 and Bank Marketing Brier score 0.0881. All six figures retain identical plotted results. B.3 corrects their attribution to the refitted predictor without changing the reported performance.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the multiplier relation to lambda=(N/n) times the KKT multiplier. Assumption 2.5 changes B>0 to B>=1; the entropy term gains an additive 1, and its covering radius changes from 1/[160B(lambda+1)^(3/2)N] to 1/[1280B(lambda+1)N]. Appendices C.1–C.3 substantially revise the population-minimizer, concentration, symmetrization, covering, and tail-integration arguments. Section 3.1 removes the selected-span entropy bound and resulting statistical-risk bound for greedy iterates, retaining Theorem 3.1’s optimization guarantee.

C1.justification: Section 1.2 drops the assertion that the greedy optimization guarantee also translates into prediction risk, consistent with the deletion in Section 3.1. The abstract, contribution bullets, and central claims about coupled training and negative transfer otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 now explicitly states that Theorem 3.1 concerns selection-stage iterates, not the post-selection refit or its test metrics. It also removes the explanation that refitting reduces greedy-stage shrinkage. The broader limitations and negative-transfer interpretations remain.

D1.justification: B.3 explicitly distinguishes the internal AFS iterates, separately trained teacher, and final ridge predictor, specifying that only the selected deployment span is retained. V1 already documented the labeled-only teacher and refit penalty of 0.001; v2 resolves ambiguity about their roles.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 slightly narrows positioning relative to greedy approximation and dictionary-learning research by claiming empirical optimization control without the previous prediction-risk extension. The cited works remain the same; reference metadata updates do not add literature.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites and retitles B.3, shortens the discussion following Theorem 3.1, and revises explanatory passages in Appendix C. These are localized changes within the retained section and appendix structure.

P2.justification: Figure 5’s caption now identifies the post-selection deployment refit and Algorithm 1’s dictionary-selection role. Mathematical typography, equation formatting, and text placement change, while the six plot graphics and two table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 repairs important theoretical gaps: C.1 replaces an unjustified projection-linearity step for convex classes with a direct minimization and uniqueness argument, while C.2–C.3 repair the concentration and covering derivations supporting the main risk bound. It also removes the unsupported extension from fixed-span complexity to adaptive greedy-iterate risk and clearly separates PneumoniaMNIST refit performance from the optimization theorem. These changes substantially improve mathematical support and evidence attribution. The narrower theoretical scope improves reliability while preserving the empirical findings.
